points.point: Division (staff, investigations, enforcement, audits) vs. Commission (rules, forms, final decisions)
Commission: 5 members appointed by the governor; 3 brokers (5 yrs' experience, one property management) + 2 public; 3-year terms
Commission rules carry the force of law; brokers must use a Commission-approved form when one exists and fits
Must respond to a complaint or audit notice in writing on time with the full file; failure is its own ground for discipline
Hearings conducted by an ALJ; denial, suspension or revocation only by majority vote of the Commission
Sanctions: fine up to $2,500 per offense, censure, probation, suspension, revocation, denial
Letter of admonition by certified mail; licensee may demand formal hearing in writing within 20 days
After revocation, no new application considered for one year
Commission can suspend or revoke a firm's right to operate regardless of the responsible broker's knowledge
Commission can seek a court injunction against anyone violating the license law
Appeals of Commission orders go to the Colorado Court of Appeals
Complaints and investigative files confidential; stipulations and final orders public
Unlicensed brokerage is a class 2 misdemeanor
Recovery fund repealed in 2005; mandatory E&O instead
Position statements are guidance, not law
Employing broker disciplined for an associate's violation only with actual knowledge or negligent supervision
Brokerage acts for compensation require a license; one transaction is enough
Exemption: attorney-in-fact only when acting without compensation
Exemption: salaried on-site manager of an apartment or condo doing customary duties
One broker license; independent broker needs 2 years Active
Employing broker: 2 years active in prior 5, experience points, 24-hour Brokerage Administration course
High level of supervision for brokers with under 2 years' experience
168 hours of pre-licensing education (48 + 48 + 72) or a real estate degree
Age 18+, exam score valid one year, fingerprints to CBI before applying
Disclose convictions, no-contest pleas, deferred judgments, pending charges with documents and explanation
No E&O proof or employing broker within 30 days of notice → license issued Inactive
Firm needs a responsible broker; temporary license up to 90 days plus one 90-day extension if that broker leaves
Licenses are personal: not transferable, can't be lent
Colorado-resident independent and employing brokers must keep a Colorado place of business
First license expires Dec 31 of year issued; then 3-year calendar cycles
Firms don't renew separately; the employing/independent broker renews
CE: 24 hours per cycle, including the 4-hour Annual Commission Update every year
Missed Annual Commission Update can't be made up; alternatives such as the 24-hour Broker Reactivation course
No CE required for the initial partial-year license period
Inactive license: still renewed, no E&O, no licensed activity, may be paid for commissions earned while Active
Inactive more than 3 years: reactivate by passing state exam or 72 hours of coursework
Automatic inactivation, including when the employing broker's license is suspended, revoked or expires
Reinstatement: 31 days–1 year = renewal fee + half
Expired more than 3 years = new applicant
Leaving or changing firms: immediate notice; no licensed work until license transfers
Written notice within 30 calendar days of a conviction, plea or deferred judgment
E&O required for Active brokers; inactive brokers (and covered attorney-licensees) exempt
Coverage via Division group plan or independent policy; individual minimums $100k/$300k, deductible ≤ $1,000
Firm-wide independent policy: $1,000,000 per claim and aggregate
E&O lapse → license Inactive immediately
Every ad shows the firm name clearly and conspicuously
One filed trade name; franchise ads need an independent-ownership statement
Team names can't include realty, real estate, company, Inc., LLC, etc.
Expired listings removed from online media within 3 days
Advertising another firm's listing requires that firm's written permission and disclosure
Employing broker supervises associates and unlicensed staff; may delegate in writing but remains responsible
Required written policies, including an office policy manual signed by every associate
Competency: decline, acquire knowledge, get help, or co-list
Associates paid only by their employing broker
No compensation to unlicensed persons
Referral fees to out-of-state brokers: actual referral, no Colorado brokerage, paid through the Colorado firm
RESPA: no fees or things of value for referring settlement services
Affiliated business arrangements disclosed at or before referral
Rebates to own client allowed: in writing, lender-approved, on the settlement statement
Secret profits barred; separate closing-service charges itemized with written consent
Net listings not expressly prohibited but discouraged
No lien or lis pendens for a disputed residential commission without a court judgment
Own-account deals: written disclosure of license status in the contract or at the same time
Buying own listing: amend/terminate listing, disclose, seller may terminate through closing
Continuing duty to disclose conflicts of interest in writing
Copies of documents given at the time prepared
Present offers to listing broker, then its employing broker, then the owner
Keep transaction files 4 years
Listings in writing before services, with a definite termination date
Holdover covers only buyers named to the seller in writing during the term
Listings belong to the firm; moving one needs seller consent and the firm's assignment
Conway-Bogue: standard forms, own transactions, no charge beyond the commission
No advice on title exceptions; recommend an attorney
No drafting custom legal language (unauthorized practice of law)
Seller financing: negotiating residential loan terms is MLO work
Lease-options/installment contracts: no approved form; involve an attorney
Promissory note as earnest money: tell seller due date; if unpaid, notify seller and deliver original
Unlicensed assistants: clerical tasks yes, negotiating or advising no
Unlicensed on-site managers: show, quote set rents, collect; no negotiating material terms
No sign crossing on an unexpired exclusive listing
Grounds for discipline highlights (e.g., acting for more than one party without everyone's knowledge)
Respond to complaints and audits on time
License suspended/inactive: stop activity; 7 days to notify; 30 days to disburse trust money
Commission jurisdiction follows the broker even as principal; disclose license status in writing in the contract
Position statements are non-binding guidance
Competency judged task by task; decline, learn, get help, or co-list
Statutory minimum duties can't be waived
Commissions negotiable; not set by law
Commission split vs. desk fee; commission always paid to the firm
Qualified real estate agent test: licensed, paid on output, written contract
Team names and firm name in team ads
Team member buying a team listing: consent to transaction-brokerage, removal, firewall
Own rental: written lease statement as owner and licensed broker
Buying own listing: terminate/amend, disclose, seller right to terminate
Disclose conflicts, e.g., vendor ties, early with an opt-out
Others' money held outside brokerage still goes to a trust account
E-signatures valid; electronic copies count as duplicates
After a relationship ends: all account for money; single agents also keep confidences

Commission composition and appointment
Disciplinary sanctions and fines
Letter of admonition: 20 days to request formal hearing
Appeals to the Colorado Court of Appeals
No recovery fund; E&O instead

Who needs a license and exemptions
License levels and employing broker qualification
Exam score validity and fingerprints; full eligibility

RESPA kickbacks and rebates
